notes.text: Cook the patties in two batches so they have room in the pan. Wash the tongs and your hands after each batch of raw beef.

move.title: Small patties, a sure middle
move.body: Köfte are small Turkish beef patties with onion, parsley, and cumin, eaten in homes all over Turkey. Today you'll shape them, cook them in a skillet, and use the thermometer to check that the middle reaches 160°F, the safe temperature for ground beef. A fresh tomato and cucumber salad goes with them.

why.title: Squeeze the onion
why.body: Thawed frozen onion is full of water. Squeezing it in a paper towel keeps the patties from turning wet and falling apart.

why.title: Small and flat
why.body: A small, flat patty cooks through quickly and evenly. A thick one browns outside long before the middle is hot.

why.title: Brown doesn't mean done
why.body: Ground beef can turn brown inside before it's safe, or stay pink after it is. Color can't tell you. Only the thermometer can.

why.title: In from the side
why.body: The thermometer reads at its tip. Push it in from the side of the patty so the tip sits in the very middle.

why.title: Wait for the number
why.body: A thermometer takes a few seconds to settle. Hold it still until the number stops climbing, then read it.

wrong.fix: Squeeze the onion drier next time. Turn them gently with the spatula, not the tongs.
Cook it 1 more minute on each side, then check again.
Turn the heat down to medium for the next batch.
Scoop out the tomato seeds next time, as you did in week 5.

quiz.q: What temperature does ground beef need?
A patty is brown all the way through. Is it done?
choices: Check it with the thermometer to know
quiz.explain: Color can't tell you. The thermometer can.

choices: In from the side, tip in the middle
quiz.explain: The tip reads, so it goes in the middle.

substitutions.note: Use the same amount of quick gluten-free oats.

steps.text: Put the frozen onion in the small bowl. Microwave it until thawed.
Tip the onion onto two paper towels. Fold them over and squeeze out the water over the sink.
steps.tip: Squeeze hard. Dry onion holds the patties together.

steps.text: Pull the parsley leaves off their stems. Tear them into small bits with your fingers.
steps.look: Bits about the size of your little fingernail.

steps.text: Put the beef, onion, parsley, panko, garlic, cumin, paprika, the köfte's salt, and the pepper in the large bowl. Mix with your hands.
steps.tip: Mix until you can't see streaks of crumbs.

steps.text: Wash your hands with soap for 20 seconds.
Peel the cucumber. Cut it in half the long way and scoop out the seeds. Slice it into half-moons.
steps.tip: Use the bridge grip for the long cut.

steps.text: Core the tomatoes and scoop out the seeds. Cut them into small wedges.
steps.look: Wedges about as big as the cucumber pieces.

steps.text: Put the cucumber and tomato in the medium bowl. Squeeze in the lemon. Add the olive oil and the salad's salt, and stir.
steps.tip: Catch the lemon seeds in your other hand.

steps.text: Wet your hands. Shape the beef into 12 small patties, each about as thick as your finger. Set them on the plate.
steps.look: 12 flat patties, all about the same size.

steps.text: Wash your hands with soap. Wipe the counter where the beef was.
Heat the oil in the skillet over medium-high heat.
Use the tongs to lay the patties in the pan. Lay each one down away from you.
steps.tip: Leave a finger's width between them.

steps.text: Put the tongs and the raw-beef plate in the sink. Wash your hands.
Let the patties cook without moving them.
steps.look: Brown edges, and they lift easily.

steps.text: Flip each patty with the spatula. Cook the other side.
Slide the thermometer into the side of the biggest patty. It should read 160°F or more. If not, cook 1 more minute.
steps.tip: Hold it still until the number stops moving.

steps.text: Turn off the stove. Wrap the pitas in a damp paper towel and microwave them until warm.
steps.tip: Open the towel slowly. The steam is hot.

steps.text: Put 3 köfte and a scoop of salad on each pita.
steps.look: Browned patties next to a bright, juicy salad.
